evidence.text: For babies who are being treated with intravenous antibiotics because of risk factors for early-onset infection or clinical indicators of possible infection, stop antibiotics at 36 hours if: • the blood culture is negative and • the initial clinical suspicion of infection was not strong and • the baby's clinical condition is reassuring, with no clinical indicators of possible infection (see box 2 for clinical indicators of possible early-onset infection) and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration are reassuring. [2012, amended 2026]

claims.text: A negative culture at 36 hours guarantees antibiotics can be stopped even when the baby still has respiratory distress.

reasons: Claim C1 is not supported: evidence requires multiple criteria (negative culture, low clinical suspicion, reassuring condition, CRP trends). The presence of ongoing respiratory distress violates the 'clinical condition is reassuring' requirement, so the claim is contradicted.

The guideline requires multiple conditions (negative culture, low initial suspicion, reassuring clinical condition, and reassuring CRP) to stop antibiotics at 36 h. The claim states a guarantee based solely on a negative culture, ignoring the need for a reassuring clinical condition, which the patient lacks (respiratory distress).
